title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Ridley Staff
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of Ridley and its controlled entities. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, the ban on short-term trading, the Specific Prohibited Periods, and the absolute ban on derivatives/hedging in section 5.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Ridley; must notify and receive written approval from the Chair before transacting (the Chair himself needs approval from the Managing Director and one other director), and must notify the Company Secretary in writing within two business days after transacting.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Members of the Executive Lead Team and any other executives designated as such by the Managing Director, including all Key Management Personnel under Australian Accounting Standards. Must notify and receive written approval from the Managing Director before transacting.

tiers.name: Close Associates
tiers.description: A family member of a director or Senior Executive who may be expected to influence or be influenced by them in dealings with Ridley Securities (spouse, de facto partner, children living at home, or dependants), or a company, trust or other entity controlled by that director or Senior Executive (alone or jointly with another Close Associate).

definitions.hedging_definition: any derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security, or any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security

windows.start_anchor: 30 June (end of the Company's financial year)

windows.end_anchor: announcement of the Company's half year results to the ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose additional Specific Prohibited Periods by written notice to all Ridley Staff at any time at its sole discretion. Notified in writing to all staff, so not confidential.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban on any derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security for every Ridley employee, director and officer. No clearance, exception or Board discretion is available; section 6's approval process governs only ordinary trading, not derivatives.
rules.evidence: Ridley employees, directors and officers must not enter into any derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security, or any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security.

rules.detail: The same section 5 sentence bans any transaction designed or intended to limit the economic risk of holding a Ridley Security, with no distinction between vested and unvested holdings and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: or any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security.

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar monetisation structure is expressly caught by the ban on transactions 'designed or intended to securitise' a Ridley Security, in addition to the general derivative ban.
rules.evidence: any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named. It would be caught only as an ordinary 'dealing' in securities, subject to the insider trading prohibition, the Specific Prohibited Periods, and (for Directors/Senior Executives) the section 6 approval process.
rules.evidence: acquires, disposes of or engages in other dealings in securities in the company

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
A CFD referencing Ridley shares is a derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security and so is expressly banned, even though CFDs are not separately named.
rules.evidence: Ridley employees, directors and officers must not enter into any derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security

rules.detail: The policy contains no provision addressing margin loans or any other financing arrangement in respect of Ridley Securities.
The policy contains no provision addressing granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Ridley Securities.
The policy contains no secured financing provision of any kind; it is silent on whether a loan secured against Ridley Securities is permitted.

Ban on short-term trading, defined as disposing of securities within 12 months of acquisition for short-term profit, applying to all Ridley Staff; disposal of shares from exercise of employee options is expressly excluded from the definition.
rules.evidence: Ridley Staff should not engage in short-term trading of Ridley Securities.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (who then notifies the ASX)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days after transacting
clearance.evidence: Directors must notify and receive approval in writing from the Chair of the intention to transact in Ridley Securities.

clearance.approver: Managing Director and one other director
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (who then notifies the ASX)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two business days after transacting
clearance.evidence: If the Chair intends to transact, he is required to secure written approval from the Managing Director and one other director.

clearance.post_trade_to: Managing Director (general 'before and after' requirement; the detailed post-trade notice procedure in 6(iii) is stated only for Directors)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: not specified beyond the general requirement to notify 'before and after any dealing'
clearance.evidence: Senior Executives must notify and receive approval in writing from the Managing Director of the intention to transact in Ridley Securities.

carve_outs: disposal of shares from the exercise of employee options
short_term.evidence: Short term trading may include trading in Ridley Securities for short-term profits, generally in circumstances where securities are disposed within 12 months of the date of acquisition.

exceptions.evidence: This Policy does not apply to trading in the securities of Ridley to the extent that such trading is an acquisition of securities of Ridley under an employee incentive scheme.
The prohibition does not apply to subscriptions for new shares made under an employee share scheme, long term incentive plan or dividend reinvestment plan.
No notification to the Company Secretary is required for acquisitions of Ridley Securities by employees under the Dividend Reinvestment Plan, Long Term Incentive Plan, or Employee Share Scheme.

exemption_authority: None. The derivative/hedging ban in section 5 is absolute, with no clearance, exception or Board discretion to permit it. The Board's only stated discretion is to impose additional Specific Prohibited Periods (section 4) or, under section 6, to approve or refuse an individual director's or Senior Executive's ordinary (non-derivative) share dealing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Ridley employees, directors and officers must not enter into any derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security, or any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a funded collar (the purchased put and the written call) are OTC derivative contracts relating to a Ridley Security, so they are prohibited outright for every Ridley Staff member with no clearance path, which alone defeats the structure regardless of financing terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (policy contains no section on margin loans, security arrangements or secured financing)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express prohibition, approval requirement or disclosure obligation for a loan secured against Ridley shares, but this is moot because the derivative legs of the collar cannot be entered into under section 5 in any event.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other transaction that is designed or intended to securitise, or limit the economic risk of holding, a Ridley Security
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This broad language would likely also catch a non-derivative monetisation structure (e.g. a prepaid forward) even if it were not technically a 'derivative contract', closing off alternative structures too.

bespoke_clauses.clause: each director and Senior Executive must take all reasonable steps to ensure that their Close Associates comply with this Policy in relation to Ridley Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a spouse, family trust or a controlled entity does not avoid the section 5 ban, since directors and Senior Executives are responsible for ensuring their Close Associates also comply.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (no hardship, court order or exceptional-circumstances carve-out is stated anywhere in the policy)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no discretion anywhere in the policy to permit a banned derivative, or to bring forward dealing during a Specific Prohibited Period, in exceptional circumstances.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy in any form. Section 5 imposes an absolute, unconditional ban on every Ridley Staff member (employees, directors and officers) entering into any derivative contract relating to a Ridley Security, or any other transaction designed or intended to securitise or limit the economic risk of holding a Ridley Security; this directly and expressly prohibits both the purchased put and written call legs of a collar, with no clearance, exception or Board discretion available anywhere in the policy. The policy is entirely silent on margin loans, security arrangements or secured financing, so while a loan secured on the shares is not itself prohibited, that is immaterial because the derivative legs cannot be entered into at all. The ban also extends to the Close Associates of Directors and Senior Executives, so the structure cannot be routed through a spouse, trust or controlled entity. There is no hardship, court order or other exceptional-circumstances carve-out from the derivative ban. No funded OTC equity collar can be offered to any Ridley director or executive under this policy as currently drafted.
